research_notes: Wellmann II 173 (p. 240). Taxonomic caveat: Dimopoulos et al. 2013 splits Greek capers into C. orientalis Veill. (most regions), C. sicula Veill. and C. zoharyi Inocencio & al. It lists C. spinosa L. s.str. with '?' in most regions and comments that it is a hybridogenous nothotaxon, mainly cultivated or feral (Inocencio & al. 2006). WCVP (and therefore POWO) instead treats all of these within C. spinosa: C. orientalis is a synonym of C. spinosa subsp. rupestris, C. sicula of var. canescens and C. zoharyi of subsp. aegyptia. C. spinosa s.l. is native in Greece, Kriti and the East Aegean. GBIF caveat: the backbone treats C. sicula, C. zoharyi and C. rupestris as synonyms of C. spinosa (speciesKey 6370689), but C. orientalis Duhamel as a SEPARATE accepted species (speciesKey 5601705). Greek occurrence records may therefore be split, and the pipeline should consider merging key 5601705.
